To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the envelope membranes of chloroplasts from leaves of spinach and pea bind 125I-cal modulin in a calcium-dependent manner.
calmodulin-binding protein is found in the chloroplast envelopes of spinach and pea leaves.
calmodulin binding was detected in chloroplast envelope membranes and that this binding was associated with a major calmodulin binding polypeptide (M(r) 33,000).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of calmodulin binding proteins and the role of calmodulin in the regulation of chloroplastic function.
the role of calmodulin in the regulation of chlorophyll biosynthesis and the effects of calmodulin on chloroplast function.
the identification and characterization of the calmodulin-binding protein(s) in the chloroplasts of higher plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a great deal of variation in the distribution of calmodulin and its binding proteins among species and tissues, and that calmodulin-binding activity in a particular tissue is not necessarily associated with a particular function or physiological role.
the chloroplast envelope membrane is a major site of calmodulation in plants.
calmodulin is present in all subcellular orga- nellar compartments, and that the calmodulin-binding protein complement varies from one subcellular organeellar fraction to another.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calmodulin is a ubiquitous protein that has a variety of functions in plants, and that the chloroplast may be a site of calmodulindirected action in plants.
calmodulin-binding protein(s) are localized in the envelope membrane of the chloroplast.
calmodulin binding is a general property of subcellular organellar membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chloroplast envelope contains a calmodulin-binding protein.
calmodulin binding is primarily associated with a 33-kDa protein in the envelope membrane of chloroplasts.
we identified a new role for calmodulin as a regulator of chloroplast envelope function, and that this role may be conserved in both higher and lower plants.
